corrected_claim.existence: For every real R>=640000, there exists a translate of the unit triangular lattice whose closed radius-R disk crop can be replaced by a unit-separated packing of at least pi*R^2/a0 + R/160000 labels, where a0=sqrt(3)/2.
corrected_claim.downstream_implication: Every global minimum-diameter n-point unit-separated set with D>1280000 satisfies g_A=n-1-pi*D^2/(2*sqrt(3)) >= D/320000.
not_established: source-specific upper bound g_A<=cD+o(D) for c<1/320000
corrected_claim.lifecycle: Candidate remains unreviewed; no canonical promotion or theorem-state change.

independent_mathematical_reconstruction.row_packet: For h=19/20, integer interval length L=B-A, insert (A+1+i*h,y+eta_i) for i=0..floor((L-2)/h), with alternating eta=1/6 and 1/2. Insertions count at least (L-2)/h; at most L+1 row labels are removed, so net gain >=(L-59)/19. L>=65 forces a positive integer net gain >=1.
independent_mathematical_reconstruction.within_and_cross_row_separation: Adjacent packet squared distance is (19/20)^2+(1/3)^2=3649/3600>1; nonadjacent horizontal gap is >=19/10. A lower lattice row is vertically >=a0+1/6>1 away. The packet stays in [A+1,B-1], endpoints are guarded, and retained same/higher-row labels have positive vertical gap and horizontal separation. The disk roof condition places every insertion in the closed disk.
independent_mathematical_reconstruction.qualifying_rows: Let delta=1/200 and f(z)=sqrt(R^2-z^2). Select lattice rows y satisfying f(delta R)<=y and y+a0<=f(delta R/2). Put u=f(y+a0), v=f(y+1/2), A=ceil(u), B=floor(v). On these arcs |f'(z)|>=sqrt(1-delta^2)/delta>199; a0-1/2>1/3. The mean-value theorem gives v-u>199/3, inward rounding loses <2, hence L>193/3>64 and integer L>=65.
independent_mathematical_reconstruction.simultaneous_rows_and_count: The roof-height bands for distinct selected rows are disjoint; f is strictly decreasing, so their horizontal intervals are disjoint. Packets remain one unit inside interval endpoints and hence distinct packets have horizontal gap at least 2. If Delta=f(delta R/2)-f(delta R), the row count K>=Delta/a0-2>=Delta-2. Rationalizing or integrating z/R gives Delta>=3*delta^2*R/8=3R/320000, hence K>=3R/320000-2>=R/160000 for R>=640000. Thus every translate gains at least that many labels, without an absolute baseline claim for every translate.
independent_mathematical_reconstruction.averaging_quantifier: Translation averaging over a fundamental parallelogram of area a0 gives mean original crop count pi*R^2/a0. Therefore at least one translate has baseline count at least the mean. Apply the uniform row replacement to that selected translate to obtain the absolute existential count.
independent_mathematical_reconstruction.global_minimum_step: For any 640000<=R<D/2, the constructed packing has diameter <=2R<D. If it had at least n labels, an n-point subset would contradict global minimality, so its integer population is <=n-1. Combining with the existential lower bound and taking R upward to D/2 gives n-1>=pi*D^2/(4a0)+D/320000=pi*D^2/(2sqrt(3))+D/320000. Strictness D>1280000 ensures the comparison interval is nonempty. Continuity justifies the limiting endpoint.
independent_mathematical_reconstruction.quantifier_review: README, TASK statement/domain, and VERIFY domain all use the same existential averaged-translate claim. The remaining sentence “every translate gains” is specifically the relative row increment, immediately distinguished from the absolute population bound supplied by averaging. I found no residual universal absolute-count wording.
